root_cause.text: In `af_alg_alloc_tsgl()`, when chaining a new scatter/gather list to a previous one that was fully filled to `MAX_SGL_ENTS`, the end-of-list marker on the last entry of the previous SGL (at index `MAX_SGL_ENTS - 1`) was not cleared before calling `sg_chain()`, causing `sg_next()` to prematurely return NULL and leading to a NULL pointer dereference in the scatterwalk.
root_cause.evidence: The patch explicitly adds `sg_unmark_end(sg + MAX_SGL_ENTS - 1)` before `sg_chain(sg, MAX_SGL_ENTS + 1, sgl->sg);` to remove the stale end marker. The CVE description confirms that a sendmsg() that fills an SGL exactly to `MAX_SGL_ENTS` marks the last entry as the end, and a subsequent sendmsg() fails to clear this marker before chaining.

bic_trace_step.reason: In `af_alg_alloc_tsgl()`, when a new SGL is allocated because the previous one is full (`sgl->cur >= MAX_SGL_ENTS`), the code calls `sg_chain(sg, MAX_SGL_ENTS + 1, sgl->sg)`. However, it does not clear the end-of-list marker (SG_END flag) from the last entry of the previous SGL (at index MAX_SGL_ENTS - 1) before chaining. This causes `sg_next()` to prematurely stop at that entry and return NULL, leading to a NULL pointer dereference in the scatterwalk. The fix would require calling `sg_unmark_end(sg + MAX_SGL_ENTS - 1)` before the chain operation, which is absent here.
